title: Soil moisture persistence after rainfall in Sahelian millet fields: a two-season sensor study

headings.text: Soil moisture persistence after rainfall in Sahelian millet fields: a two-season sensor study

key_sentences: We measured volumetric soil moisture at three depths in twelve smallholder millet fields over the 2024 and 2025 rainy seasons.
Moisture at 30 cm persisted above the wilting threshold for a median of 6.8 days after events larger than 20 mm, against 2.1 days after smaller events.
These results suggest that sowing advice keyed to cumulative rainfall should give more weight to the size of individual events.
Such rules treat a single heavy storm and several light showers as equivalent, although their effect on the root zone may differ widely.
Mulching lengthened persistence in every size class, with the largest gain after medium events of 10 to 20 mm.
A sowing rule based on cumulative rainfall would therefore trigger sowing in conditions that differ greatly in risk.
Even so, the agreement between seasons suggests that the relation between event size and persistence is robust enough to inform extension advice.
